links.outcome: Answer flip rate under meaning-preserving paraphrases of chest X-ray questions across nine VLMs
links.effect: Flip rates from 3% to 37% across nine VLMs; some low-flip models stay consistent even with image removed, suggesting reliance on language priors.
links.quote: Across nine VLMs, including general-purpose models, we find flip rates from 3% to 37%.

links.outcome: Consistency of VLM responses across equivalent paraphrased questions
links.effect: Flip rates of 3% to 37% across nine VLMs on meaning-preserving paraphrases; clamping a framing-related feature reduced flip rates by 31% relative.
links.quote: Medical Vision Language Models (VLMs) can change their answers when clinicians rephrase the same question, a failure mode that threatens deployment safety.

unlisted_practices: Sparse autoencoder feature clamping at inference to reduce paraphrase sensitivity (31% relative flip reduction, 1.3 percentage-point accuracy cost)
Text-only (image-removed) baselines to test visual grounding alongside paraphrase stability

screen.reason: Empirically benchmarks paraphrase sensitivity across medical VLMs and tests an inference-time guardrail (feature activation clamping) to mitigate flips.
